newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar ends flat in light trading.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar ends flat in light trading.

text.p: * Canada's dollar ended flat in light trading on Tuesday at C$1.3750 (US$0.7272) as investors gauged the financial repercussions of Monday's general election, traders said.
* They said the slim victory by the governing Liberals would have a short-term neutral effect on the currency.
* Attention now turns to U.S. non-farm payrolls data on Friday.
The Canada dollar benefited early in the session as investors showed bought the unit on the crosses. But it lost ground after a round of profit-taking, traders said.
They cautioned that interest in the Canada unit would likely remain muted ahead of Friday's U.S. non-farm payrolls report.
A Reuters survey of economists forecast May non-farm payrolls to rise by 221,000.
"Now, of course, we are going to go cautiously into non-farm payrolls on Friday," said Stephen Wateridge, managing director of corporate foreign exchange with CIBC Wood Gundy in Toronto.

On the crosses, the Canadian dollar fell to 84.29 yen from Monday's close of 84.76 yen and slid to 1.2549 marks from Monday's 1.2586 marks on news that a row between Germany's Bundesbank and the German government over gold revaluation ended in a compromise.

German Chancellor Helmut Kohl's center-right coalition government agreed with the Bundesbank on a plan to revalue central bank gold reserves in 1997, but not make any profit transfer to government coffers until next year.
The move had been hotly contested by the central bank and opposition parties, provoking a bitter mini-crisis in Germany.
